I farm this year the way I trust from long experience in Quzhou County: I keep the full 10.7 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because I have well irrigation and that system fits my land, my habits, and my household labor. Since some family labor is tied up off-farm, I keep the plan steady and practical rather than complicated. For wheat, I use an improved variety, put on solid nitrogen with enough phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate a few key times, and do rotary tillage because I want a clean, even seedbed going into the winter crop. For summer maize, I plant the same 10.7 mu after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and use no-tillage to save time and labor after the wheat comes off. I do basic pest and disease control on both crops, not excessive but enough to protect yield. My goal is stable output and lower risk, not gambling on a fancy change.
